name: Trident Care
desc:
Medical Billing Representative | $16 - $19/hr | Data Entry/Admin, No Sales Expectations
Company: TridentCare
Industry: Medical Billing / Healthcare Administration
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 You'd be behind the scenes making sure medical claims are accurate before they go out the door. That means reviewing patient logs and claims for accuracy, verifying details against the medical record, and updating patient or insurance information when something's missing or outdated. You'd also reach out directly to clients or insurance companies to track down missing information or secure pre-authorizations, and you'd cross-train across a few different billing work queues so you can handle whatever comes your way. It's steady, detail-driven desk work that keeps the whole billing process accurate and moving.
assessment: Based on similar TridentCare administrative roles, the process is interview-based rather than test-based.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
 Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent
Required Experience: None strictly required
Preferred Experience: Not specified
Required Skills:
Intermediate communication skills
Intermediate computer skills
Intermediate time management
Intermediate customer service skills
Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
A true entry level candidate, since only a high school diploma is required
Someone detail oriented who enjoys accuracy focused, behind the scenes work
A self-starter who can stay motivated without a lot of hand-holding
Someone comfortable cross-training across multiple billing systems and workflows
Not a Good Fit for
Anyone who prefers a role centered on live customer conversations over documentation and claims review
Anyone who cannot work occasional required overtime to meet department goals
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
Medical billing
Claims processing
CPT and ICD-10 codes
Insurance pre-authorization
Patient records
Data accuracy
Healthcare administration
Time management
Customer service
Detail oriented
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
Application
Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you
If the assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen
If the phone screen passes, expect a final interview
Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3 to 15 days on average.
4-5 interview questions for this role:
Tell us about a time you caught an error or inconsistency in paperwork before it became a bigger problem.
How do you stay organized when managing multiple tasks and deadlines at once?
Walk us through how you'd handle contacting a client or insurance company to get missing information.
What's your comfort level learning new systems or cross-training across different work areas?
Describe a time you worked independently without needing a lot of guidance to get the job done.
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: $16 to $19 per hour
Shift: Full-time, specific hours not listed in the posting, required overtime as needed to meet departmental goals
Benefits: Two weeks of vacation, health insurance starting after 30 days, sick time, 8 paid holidays, same-day pay availability, a medical insurance allowance to customize coverage, dental, vision, disability, company-paid life insurance, and 401(k)
Equipment Provided: Not specified in the posting, and no internet requirement is listed either. Confirm both during the recruiter screen
Felony Friendly?: Not stated
Drug Test: Not stated
Notes: This is a strong true entry level opportunity with only a high school diploma required, and the benefits package is a nice standout, especially health insurance kicking in after just 30 days and the flexibility of a medical insurance allowance. This is a good match for a participant who wants steady, detail-focused administrative work and is open to learning medical billing from the ground up.
Career Pathway: Medical Billing Representative → Senior Medical Biller → Billing Supervisor or Reimbursement Specialist
training: discussed in interview/ofer stage. must be available for any shift
